title: autumnal-sampler-profile-compiler-and-cost-rulebook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a profile compiler that generates tenant-prefill defaults and quantization suggestions; introduces a cost-rulebook DSL and simulator. Backwards compatible; opt-in via tenant flags.
description:
Motivation: customers keep asking for better out-of-the-box batching/caching/quant defaults for new workloads without manual tuning. Current defaults are conservative and require manual profiling. This PR introduces the Autumnal Sampler Profile Compiler: an offline compiler that consumes sampled request traces, runs a lightweight simulation of batching + KV cache heuristics, and outputs per-tenant "starter profiles" (batch shapes, cache TTLs, preferred quant profiles). It also introduces a small cost-rulebook DSL that encodes unit-econ constraints (e.g. max-cost-per-token, latency percentile SLO, fallthrough quantization tiers). The goal is automation-first: produce safe, measurable defaults developers can opt-in to, and provide reproducible artifacts for audits.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a new CLI/service: sampler-compiler which accepts a workload signature (trace snapshots or synthetic generator) and a rulebook; it outputs JSON profiles that can be imported into tenant defaults.
- Introduces cost-rulebook DSL (YAML): expressive but constrained: cost caps, latency targets, hard constraints (no quant below X for regulatory tenants), and fallback chains.
- Adds a simulator that computes expected per-token cost, p95 latency, and expected tail hit-rate for prefix/KV cache. Simulator uses conservative microbench kernels measured from nightly infra.
- Adds a quant-profile suggester: given model family + sequence distribution, suggests 8-bit/4-bit quant variants and marks if a profile requires runbook approval.
- Telemetry: emits a ProfileDraft.created event with anonymized signature, simulated metrics, and a deterministic provenance hash.
- Export/import plumbing: admin API endpoints (internal) for uploading generated profiles to tenant defaults and for dry-run evaluation.

Checklist: 
- [x] CLI and service implementation
- [x] rulebook parser + schema validation
- [x] simulator with unit tests and small realistic data fixtures
- [x] quant suggester and quant safety checks
- [x] telemetry events and provenance hashes
- [x] docs/quickstart and examples in redwood-quickstarts
- [x] integration tests in econ-sim-suite

Backward compatibility and safety:
- Compiler output is purely opt-in. Nothing changes tenant defaults unless an admin imports a profile.
- Rulebook enforces hard constraints; the simulator flags any profile that violates cost or latency hard guards. Those flagged profiles are marked as "requires-approval".
- Quant suggestions respect tenant-level regulatory tags in the input signature; we added an explicit "cannot-quantize-below" flag for regulated tenants.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag autumnal_sampler_compiler_enabled=false (default off).
2) Roll out telemetry and simulator in staging; collect CI-sim reported deltas.
3) Enable CLI for SRE and solutions engineers to generate first wave of starter profiles for low-risk tenants.
4) After 2 weeks of monitoring, enable import pipeline for >95% automated apply for tenants marked "auto-apply-starter-profiles".

Performance note: on a 100k-sample trace the local simulator runs in ~35s; typical tenant traces (1–5k samples) run under 8s. Simulated p95 improvements of auto-generated profiles in our internal benchmark suite show median unit-cost reduction of 16% and 95th percentile latency change within +-5ms for conversational workloads (see commits/benchmarks below).

Security/Compliance: provenance hash and anonymization are mandatory; raw input traces are not sent to hosted telemetry. The import API requires admin scope.

Related: ENG-4820 (profile compiler epic), ENG-4832 (quant safety policy).

Notes for reviewers: focus on simulator assumptions (simulator/README) and rulebook schema. I added a simple DSL parser — it prefers explicit semantics over magic defaults so we can reason about policy later.
commit_summary:
1) Implement CLI/service scaffolding and storage backend (sampler-compiler)
2) Add rulebook DSL schema and parser with tests
3) Implement simulation kernels and tie to nightly microbench constants
4) Quant suggester and safety checks with policy hooks
5) Admin API endpoints + import dry-run
6) Telemetry events and provenance hashing
7) Quickstart example and docs updates in redwood-quickstarts
8) Integration tests in econ-sim-suite
review_comments: Amit Rao: Simulator looks good but I'm concerned about the microbench constants being read from nightly; can we pin to a stable snapshot for the dry-run?
Maya Chen (author): Added a stable_snapshot param to simulator; default remains nightly but dry-run uses stable snapshot if provided. See simulator.go (line ~172).
Liam O'Connor: Rulebook DSL seems expressive. Suggest adding a 'max-quant-drop' guard so we don't jump from fp16->4bit without passing intermediate checks.
Maya Chen: Added max-quant-drop and an automatic staged-suggestion (fp16->8bit->4bit) in quant/suggester.go. Also added tests for staged rollback behavior.
Priya Singh: CI flake on first run exposed a race in profile_import_handler's memcache; suggested atomic write.
Maya Chen: Fixed with atomic replace and added a deterministic retry (exponential backoff) in admin import handler.

Detailed CSV attached in commit 3 (benchmarks/2026-02-autumnal.csv).
